findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is visible to anyone with EC2 API access or instance metadata access, and is also persisted unencrypted in Terraform state.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (the setting is explicitly commented out), leaving data at rest unencrypted and increasing exposure risk if the underlying storage or its snapshots are compromised or shared.
The EBS snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of its source volume, resulting in an unencrypted snapshot that could expose sensitive data if the snapshot is copied, shared, or made public.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management interface of the instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with unrestricted egress to all destinations, which combined with the public subnet placement significantly increases the attack surface of the instance.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, which combined with the permissive security group directly exposes the web host to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, expanding the attack surface for future resources placed here.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used for VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to network traffic metadata.
